title: StarRocks scale-up: vertical VM resize (RAM) on a BE
description: The nexus-cli scale-up verb (vertical CPU/RAM/disk resize). Demonstrates the generic vmrun stop -> .vmx memsize edit -> start flow on sr-be-3 (6 GB -> 8 GB). Cluster-aware: a BE whose tablets have replicas on the other 2 BE can be resized with no query impact.

observe.what: current RAM ~6000 MB (the right-sized 6 GB BE, vms.yaml)
graceful BE shutdown; its tablets stay served by replicas on sr-be-1/2
.vmx memsize rewritten to 8192 MB; VM powered back on

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.36 'free -m | awk "/Mem:/ {print \$2}"'; ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.31 "mysql --skip-ssl -h 127.0.0.1 -P 9030 -u root -p$SR_ROOT_PW -N -e 'SHOW BACKENDS' | grep 192.168.10.36"

observe.what: RAM now ~8192 MB AND sr-be-3 rejoined Alive=true -- vertical resize complete + cluster healthy

whatProves: scale-up resizes a BE's RAM via the generic vmrun stop -> .vmx edit -> start path; the BE cleanly rejoins. Cluster-aware: replicas on the other BE keep queries served during the resize.
